"Include statuses" probably also doesn't make sense if the report didn't have any attached statuses too?

issue_context.title: Report interface actions: duplicate actions
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

The report interface has a "quick actions" style list of actions to take against the reported user. It would be great if those action buttons indicated if they were useless. In particular, the **"Limit"** action is offered even when the user is already limited.

Additionally, even after pressing the button, there is no reaction to indicate what is going on: are limited users getting an additional notification? Did just nothing happen (while the moderator expected to take a siginificant action)?

### Expected behaviour

Don't show the button / show it greyed out indicating that the user is already limited.

### Actual behaviour

Button is available and gives no feedback after pressing it that anything is amiss.

### Specifications

v3.5.3
comments: I only reported the bug, I don't know how issue assignments work in this project. I'd assume that you can just work on it and open a PR!
I am going to leave this alone for now.
Are you meaning something like this?

Alternatively, we could hide it entirely.

(Though, I'm currently toying with an idea to do away with the quick-actions in favour of a dialog based flow, where you click "take action" and it pops up a modal on the page that's some sort of combination between custom and the predefined actions, so there's no page navigation involved — though this would need javascript, so would need to be done with progressive enhancement)

review_comments: Arguably disable and sensitive don't really make sense for accounts already suspended either?
Arguably, yes, but also, I suppose you may want to e.g. suspend the account, then apply one of those restrictions, and finally roll back that the suspend.
Maybe, but then would you just freeze?
